pg:https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2.desc: As Jean-Luc Picard in seven seasons, four films and a sequel, Stewart made us believe the most interesting person in the room might also be the most humane
paras: What might humanity look like in 400 years’ time if we really do become wiser and more compassionate with each passing decade? The creators of Star Trek: The Next Generation clearly felt the answer closely resembled Patrick Stewart, who has died aged 86 after a short illness. Their decision may well have opened up an entirely new future for Gene Roddenberry’s enduring, resolutely utopian space saga.

The bald, cerebral Englishman was a bold choice to succeed Shatner’s swaggering Canadian alpha male – but his ability to bring quiet authority and conviction to even the most outlandish of scenes gave the Enterprise an entirely different centre of gravity. Through seven seasons and four feature films, Stewart made audiences believe that the most interesting person in the room might also be the most thoughtful and humane.

Stewart also gave Star Trek an emotional scale to match the extravagance of its ideas. In the 1992 episode The Inner Light, an alien probe from a long-dead civilisation entrusts Picard with decades of another man’s existence so that it might live on in his memory. He acquires a wife, children and a whole domestic life, even entering old age, before suddenly awakening aboard his ship to discover that only minutes have passed. The premise has something of Borges about it, an entire existence unfolding in a few minutes. Stewart makes us feel the weight of years that nobody else aboard the Enterprise has lived; he later called it his favourite episode.

pg:https://www.popsci.com/science/perman.desc: The 'Sunshine Protection Act' would leave children in the dark.
paras: Add Popular Science (opens in a new tab) Daylight Saving Time (DST) has always been contentious. In the United States, the debate resurfaces almost as regularly as everyone shifts their clocks backwards in the fall and forward in the spring. Earlier this year, the U.S. House of Representatives even passed a bill called the “Sunshine Protection Act” to make DST permanent. However, the legislation hasn’t progressed much further since July, and we are mere days away from falling back.

That’s for the best, according to a team of biologists at the University of Washington, Seattle (UW). In a study published today in the journal Current Biology, researchers contend a permanent DST would needlessly endanger countless children around the country during their morning school commutes.

De la Iglesia and his colleagues explained that while most DST chatter centers on how much light is available during evening hours, it ignores the early morning consequences. Most children in the U.S. return home from school before sundown with or without DST, but a permanent shift could make predawn commutes a regular occurrence around the country. According to de la Iglesia’s team, authors of the Sunrise Protection Act didn’t factor in these issues before the school day when crafting their bill.

pg:https://variety.com/2026/tv/global/ru.desc: Russell Brand's defense in his London rape trial was "a lot of half-truths" that were "spun into lies," the prosecution said in its closing argument.

Brand has been charged with with three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault. He has pleaded not guilty to all charges. Beginning her closing argument on Friday, prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC underlined that the women in the case are not seeking “the limelight” or “any kind of publicity,” according to Sky News. pg:https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/fea.desc: The Release Notes include info about the release of a new set, as well as clarifications and rulings involving that set's cards.

pg:https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ck8.desc: Erin Patterson argued her trial was unfair due to seven grounds but three appeal judges dismissed them all.
paras: Erin Patterson, 52, was found guilty of murdering three relatives and attempting to kill another when she served them a toxic mushroom-laced meal in 2023. Her life sentence included a non-parole period of 33 years.

In Victoria's Court of Appeal on Friday, three judges threw out her appeal against her convictions and agreed with the prosecution that her sentence was inadequate, as it allowed for the possibility of freedom.
Patterson's crimes were "extraordinarily cold and calculated" and had to be "denounced in the strongest terms," they said.

pg:https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world.desc: British actor Patrick Stewart, best known for his roles in Star Trek and X-Men, has died at 86 following a battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia.
paras: British actor Patrick Stewart, best known for his roles in Star Trek and X-Men, has died at 86 following a battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia.
Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the Star Trek and X-Men franchises, has died at his home in Los Angeles. He was 86.
His death on Wednesday (Oct 28) came after a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsf.desc: Flávio Bolsonaro vows to continue father's political fight in Brazil
paras: Flávio Bolsonaro says he will continue defending his father’s political agenda. He urges supporters to remain strong and backs Rogério Marinho for president of Brazil’s Federal Senate.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: The move threatens to further strain relations between Brazilian President Lula and his Argentinian counterpart, Milei.
paras: Brazil has summoned Argentina’s top diplomat in the country to answer questions about right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, who fled first to Argentina, then to the United States, after losing Sunday’s presidential election.
On Thursday, Brazil’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called in Argentina’s charge d’affaires, Maria Emilia Cortes, sources inside the government told the news agency Reuters.

Argentina’s Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno, however, has denied on social media that his government received a formal request for explanations regarding Bolsonaro’s decision to flee into Argentina late on Tuesday.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/football/.desc: Join Billy Munday for the latest news and buildup to Saturday’s action, including Chelsea v Manchester United
paras: Mac Allister’s sense of responsibility extends to implementing Iraola’s instructions for his new team. Figures from Opta show the midfielder is winning more tackles per Premier League game this season – 2.3 on average compared to 1.8 last season; winning more duels (4.8 from 3.8); winning more aerial duels (0.9 from 0.6) and winning more possession (5.6 on average compared to 3.8).

He is sacrificing the offensive side of his game to bring more aggression and organisation to the defensive aspect, and his touches in the opposition box, chances created, goals and assists are all down on last season as a consequence. Not that Iraola is complaining.
Inter and Milan this week unveiled plans for their new stadium that will replace San Siro from the 2031-32 season, in time for Italy to co-host Euro 2032.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: Authorities ​are struggling to find a way to control the ⁠outbreak, with no approved treatments or vaccines.
paras: The death ⁠toll ⁠from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 5,000, government data ⁠show, with authorities yet to find a way to control the ⁠country’s deadliest outbreak of the virus on record.
Ebola has infected more than 10,000 people in the DRC since the outbreak was declared in May.
There are no approved treatments or vaccines to combat the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus, responsible for the ongoing outbreak.

pg:https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c.desc: The Spanish PM is hit by a succession of crises just weeks before a snap general election.
paras: It is just nine months since two trains crashed near Cordoba, killing 46 people. Now 69 bodies have been recovered here in central Spain, from wreckage strewn over the tracks and down an embankment.

But it is also a national disaster that has shattered confidence in the country's rail network and the Socialist-led government of Pedro Sánchez. It is playing out just weeks before the snap general election he called.
The formal investigation into the Toledo train disaster has only just been launched but the government has been quick to take control of the narrative.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: As people suffering post-traumatic stress watch history repeat itself, experts call for investment in safety.
paras: Madrid, Spain – “I survived but the mental scars are still there all these years later. We must stop more accidents happening,” says Cristobal Gonalez.

Gonzalez suffered multiple injuries when a high-speed train, which should have been travelling at 80 kilometres per hour (50 miles per hour), hurtled off the line at 200km/h (125mph), killing 80 people.
The accident in 2013 at Angrois, near Santiago de Compostela in northwestern Spain, remains Spain’s deadliest rail crash.

pg:https://news.un.org/en/story/2026/10/.desc: More than 28 million people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are not getting enough to eat and the number is expected to tick up in the coming months, according to the latest alert from the IPC global food security monitor.
paras: More than 28 million people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are not getting enough to eat and the number is expected to tick up in the coming months, according to the latest alert from the IPC global food security monitor.

The DRC continues to confront a severe food security crisis due to persistent conflict in the east, widespread displacement, an expanding Ebola outbreak, economic shocks and the potential impacts of the El Niño weather pattern.
The IPC is a UN-backed platform that uses a five-phase scale to classify the severity of food insecurity, with level 5 being famine.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/sport/202.desc: The 15th amateur to challenge Littler in Netflix stream on Friday evening, Sherrock was ‘lost for words’ after winning £501,000 prize
paras: On one of the biggest nights of the year for British TV, Netflix, too, there was much at stake: not just £501,000 to any of the 20 amateur challengers who managed to beat Littler in a single leg of darts, but also the jeopardy of whether audiences would choose to watch the streamer’s first UK live entertainment event – or the final of BBC juggernaut Celebrity Traitors.

Netflix also had no idea when or whether world champion Littler would be beaten at the packed event at Manchester Central arena, hosted by Gary Lineker and Richard Osman, so had put in place contingency plans to have a second place competition should Littler lose within the first few rounds.

However, watched by hundreds of his fans, “the Nuke” comfortably beat a range of contestants of differing abilities who had queued up to take part in heats during the summer, including 14-year-olds Mackinley Cooper-Johnson and Jayden Walker.

pg:https://www.bbc.com/sport/darts/artic.desc: Fallon Sherrock defeats reigning world champion Luke Littler in one leg of darts to win £501,000.
paras: Fallon Sherrock says she was "happy to overcome all the hate" after beating reigning world champion Luke Littler in one leg of darts on Friday to win £501,000.
Broadcast live globally on Netflix, Beat Luke Littler featured a host of players taking on world number one Littler in one-leg face-offs at Manchester Central.

Players could not be members of the PDC Tour, meaning Sherrock - who became the first female player to beat a male opponent at the PDC World Championship on her way to the last 32 in December 2019 - was allowed to compete.

paras: Deaths in Congo’s Ebola outbreak have topped 5,000 as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease and cases are recorded in other African countries, the latest government data on Saturday shows.

Data from the Congolese Ministry of Health showed that the disease has killed 5,026 people out of 10,351 infected, at a nearly 50% lethality rate. The surge is sparking concerns among experts regarding the authorities’ ability to contain the deadly virus.
The latest outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, was declared in mid-May, catching authorities by surprise. They have since struggled to manage it.

pg:https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cq5.desc: Xi's anti-corruption campaign has become "an effort to consolidate and maintain authority", observers say.
paras: The fifth plenum was attended by 279 Central Committee members, compared to 315 at the fourth plenum in October 2025 and 364 at the third one in July 2024.
While recent plenums focused on economic reforms or social and development issues, party discipline took centre stage at this week's gathering.
Xi Jinping has made the fight against corruption a central pillar of his rule since he took the reins in 2012, calling it the "biggest threat" to the party.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/world/202.desc: The unprecedented number of empty seats at the political meeting – a symbol of expulsions – indicates the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping
paras: China expelled a record number of officials from the Chinese Communist party (CCP) as it concluded a major political gathering, which saw an unprecedented number of empty seats indicating the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping.
A record 33 members were expelled at this week’s fifth plenum, a gathering of top officials that takes place roughly once a year.

Just 279 of the full and alternate members of the CCP’s Central Committee attended this week’s gathering, compared with the 376 originally named as members in 2022. That means that more than 25% of the original cohort were absent, many due to purges. It is the highest number of “empty chairs” at the plenum in modern Chinese history.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: Deal would be one of the most significant steps to supply defensive weapons to Kyiv since ​Trump took office in 2025.
paras: The United States says it has approved the possible sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles to Ukraine ⁠for an estimated $2.1bn.

The package of missiles, parts and support, announced on Friday by the US State Department, would be one of the most significant steps to supply defensive weapons to Kyiv since the start of the second administration of President Donald Trump in January 2025.

Delayed missile deliveries, however, have stoked US-Ukraine tensions after Trump announced a diesel deal ⁠with Russia and criticised Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for his unwillingness to stop attacks on Russian refineries.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026.desc: Makhachev, one of the best fighters in UFC history, wants to face the winner of next year's Prates vs Morales fight.
paras: Reigning UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev has hinted at an imminent retirement, saying his next fight will be “one of the last” of his mixed martial arts career.
The Russian-born Dagestani fighter has expressed a desire to face the winner of the upcoming bout between Carlos Prates and Michael Morales in a bid to prove to the world “who is the best”.

Makhachev (29 wins, one loss) successfully defended his UFC welterweight championship belt in August, defeating ‌‌Ireland’s Ian Machado Garry via unanimous decision in the main event of UFC 330 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

pg:https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c.desc: Residents were taken out from the devastated city on Friday during a local ceasefire.
paras: Residents evacuated from the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have arrived in Belarus and are expected back in Ukraine later on Saturday, authorities have said.
They were taken out on Friday during a local ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump.
Planes carrying Oleshky residents landed in the city of Gomel on Saturday morning, according to Belarusian state media and a senior Ukrainian official.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: Four planes transporting evacuees from the war-ravaged city have arrived in Belarus's Gomel.
paras: Hundreds of residents from the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky have been transported to Belarus, as part of a major evacuation mission under a truce that the White House says United States First Lady Melania Trump helped broker.
Four planes carrying the Oleshky evacuees arrived in the southeastern Belarusian town of Gomel on Saturday, said Ukrainian parliament member David Arakhamia.
The group was met in Gomel by rescue workers, medical teams and Red Cross volunteers, Belarusian state media reported.

pg:https://www.npr.org/2026/10/30/g-s1-1.desc: Israel's consequential election has ended in a deadlock, with neither side able to claim a majority, What happens now?
paras: Israeli left-wing activists call for a government with Arab parties outside Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot's residence in Herzliya, Israel, Thursday. David Goldman/AP hide caption

TEL AVIV, Israel — Israel's election has produced a political deadlock, leaving neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, with a clear path to forming a government.

The final results announced Friday give opposition parties more seats than Netanyahu's right-wing bloc. But Eisenkot, a center-right former military chief of staff, cannot reach a governing majority without the support of predominantly Arab parties — an option Eisenkot's allies repeatedly ruled out during the campaign.

pg:https://www.bbc.com/sport/mixed-marti.desc: UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev says his next fight will be "one of the last" of his illustrious career.
paras: UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev says his next fight will be "one of the last" of his illustrious career.
The 35-year-old Russian beat Ian Machado Garry in August to defend his welterweight title in a 17th-straight victory in the UFC.
The win meant Makhachev, who is a former lightweight world champion, broke Anderson Silva's 13-year record for the longest win streak in UFC history.

pg:https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ck1.desc: Andreas Malm was due to appear on a panel alongside a co-founder of the proscribed group next week.
paras: Andreas Malm told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that he had received a letter from the Home Office notifying him that his presence was "not conducive to the public good", with no further details given.
He said he could not "see any other explanation" for being denied entry than his scheduled appearance with Huda Ammori, a founder of the group, which is a proscribed terrorist organisation in the UK.

Malm is a senior lecturer in human ecology at Sweden's Lund University, whose work includes the 2021 book How to Blow up a Pipeline and 2025's The Destruction of Palestine is the Destruction of the Earth.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2.desc: Swedish author was due to speak alongside Palestine Action co-founder at event discussing ban on the group
paras: Andreas Malm, the climate academic and author of How to Blow Up a Pipeline, has been blocked from entering the UK before he was due to speak alongside a co-founder of the banned group Palestine Action.
Malm was told by immigration officials his presence in the UK “may not be considered to be conducive to the public good”. He said the decision was “scandalous” and urged the government to reconsider.

Malm, an associate professor of human ecology at Lund University in Sweden, was due to headline a conference organised by Tribune magazine next week on “Washington’s global reign of terror and Britain’s role in reinforcing it”.

pg:https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/w.desc: Israel's opposition bloc is considering legislation to introduce direct elections for prime minister in a bid to break the political deadlock following Tuesday's inconclusive election and potentially form a minority government without relying on Arab parties, according to The Times of Israel.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/world/202.desc: Critics cite Lana Nusseibeh’s denial of accusations the UAE is fuelling Sudan war by supporting paramilitary RSF
paras: Members of the Sudanese diaspora and international human rights monitors have denounced the candidature of an Emirati diplomat for the top job at the UN, citing her denial of accusations that the United Arab Emirates is fuelling the war in Sudan by supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.
The UAE nominated Lana Nusseibeh last week to replace the UN secretary general, António Guterres, as he finishes his second five-year term ⁠this year, upending a race that had become gridlocked.

Rights groups and others have for years documented evidence of UAE support for the RSF, which has been accused of atrocities during the course of its war against the Sudanese army, including an attack on the city of El Fasher in October 2025 that the UN said had “hallmarks of genocide”.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1.desc: Poland’s centrist government says it is restoring judicial independence after years of far-right political interference.
paras: Riot police have been deployed outside Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal as a dispute over who should serve on the court escalates into a confrontation between Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s government and the nationalist opposition.

Hundreds of protesters gathered outside the Warsaw building on Friday night after judges elected by the current parliamentary majority announced the suspension of the tribunal’s president, Bogdan Swieczkowski, and his deputy, Bartlomiej Sochanski.

The move drew condemnation from the far-right opposition Law and Justice party, known as PiS, and prompted President Karol Nawrocki, a PiS ally, to abandon a trip to Senegal, turning his plane around to return to Poland on Friday. Police said three people were arrested after trying to enter the court complex.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/business/.desc: There is no end in sight for the drivers of illegal mining, while police action appears ineffective
paras: Cora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area.

In late September, dozens of zama zamas – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa, meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led Animal Welfare).

Soon, they were taking water for their panning and processing from the organisation’s two 25,000-litre water tanks, which are filled irregularly by the city government for the 100 or so rescued and injured animals on site.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026.desc: Arsenal, second in the table, travel to Anfield looking to bounce back from their shock League Cup fourth-round exit.
paras: Humiliated by one of the most chastening defeats in their club’s glittering history, Arsenal have a chance to erase the embarrassment of their League Cup loss at Fleetwood Town when they face Premier League title rivals Liverpool on Sunday.
Mikel Arteta’s side were left shell-shocked by their penalty shootout exit against fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood following a dismal display in Tuesday’s 1-1 draw.

The Premier League champions were so far below their best that it was hard to believe this was the same team that stormed to the title last term and looked hungry to retain the crown in the opening weeks of this season.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/world/202.desc: Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website
paras: Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country.
Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt.
According to Mada Masr, Attalah was released after the news outlet had paid a fine of 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100), prompting statements of support from global human rights groups.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/environme.desc: Turkey has been hit by powerful thunderstorms and a fatal tornado this week with more heavy rain expected
paras: Heavy rain and strong winds will continue to affect parts of south-eastern Europe and Turkey over the next few days, as an area of low pressure in the region has allowed for the formation of powerful thunderstorms. During a particularly intense thunderstorm in Antalya, a coastal city in the south-west of Turkey, the formation of a tornado resulted in the deaths of four construction workers on Tuesday. Authorities in Greece and Turkey have released severe rainfall and flooding warnings, as a further 100-150mm (nearly 4-6in) of rain is expected this week in central Greece and western parts of Turkey, with locally higher totals possible.

Travelling eastwards towards south Asia, strong winds and heavy rainfall have swept across the Indian regions of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh as Cyclone Arnab made landfall. With wind gusts in excess of 85mph (140km/h) and rainfall totals in some regions exceeding 200mm, the severe storm has prompted mass evacuations of more than 180,000 people, as well as widespread disruption to energy and transport infrastructure. The cyclone will weaken as it continues to traverse northwards over the coming days, though will continue to deliver heavy rain to parts of northern and central India as it does so.

Heading towards the western Pacific Ocean, Typhoon In-fa was upgraded on Wednesday to super typhoon status, with exceptionally strong sustained wind speeds of 150mph (240km/h), with winds gusting over 185mph (296km/h). Travelling north-westwards, it is expected to avoid Guam, which was hammered by Typhoon Champi earlier this month. However, In-fa is expected to affect the Mariana Islands, which have already been battered by four super typhoons this year alone.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/world/202.desc: Brazilian media ridicule defeated candidate over ‘shameful’ absconsion to US and bizarre letter with wrong coat of arms
paras: Flávio Bolsonaro had hoped that by Sunday night people would be calling him the next president of Brazil.

Instead, the far-right politician’s decision to flee to the US after losing the election and – for 58 minutes – to declare himself “Brazil’s true president-elect”, has made him a laughing stock, with Brazilian newspapers and commentators raining a barrage of scornful adjectives down on the conquered candidate.

Bolsonaro fled to Miami on Tuesday night, 48 hours after being beaten by his leftwing adversary, the incumbent president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, by 4.4m votes. Lula’s victory has been recognised by rightwing leaders from around the world, including El Salvador’s Nayib Bukele and Italy’s Giorgia Meloni, not to mention Bolsonaro’s own party and many key allies.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/world/202.desc: Musician wrote a ‘love letter’ to Canada with a new album – and some pointed commentary about the US president
paras: Lake Ontario, the vast body of water that straddles the US-Canada border, has gone by many names over the centuries: Lac Saint-Louis, Lacus Ontarius, Skaniadorio, Cataraqui Lake. But one thing it will never be called, says the Canadian rock star Bryan Adams, is Lake America.
In his new song Lake Ontario, Adams takes aim at the US president, Donald Trump, accusing him of “breaking the peace” between the people who live on the lake’s shores.

Trump signed an executive order in August directing US federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario “Lake America”, echoing his earlier, widely mocked decision to rename the Gulf of Mexico “the Gulf of America”.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/world/202.desc: The trouncing of the far right provides a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France
paras: Thank you, Brazil, for demonstrating how the far right can be trounced while protection for the Amazon is strengthened. In a world where nature and democracy appeared to be bleeding out in tandem, voters and forest defenders in this global south powerhouse have shown it is possible to staunch the flow. This should provide much needed inspiration and, more practically, a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France.

Coming just weeks after the Lula administration announced a record fall in Amazon and Cerrado destruction, they hope Brazil can now go on to achieve its target of zero deforestation by 2030 and continue to support a global transition away from fossil fuels. That would provide a huge boost to flagging global efforts to stabilise the climate and protect degraded ecosystems. It would also set a remarkable example of leadership by the global south.

Big battles lie ahead. In the Amazon region itself, far-right members of Bolsonaro’s party have won the governorships of seven of the nine states and a large number of municipal mayorships. Brazil’s congress is now dominated by agribusiness and mining interests that have set the political agenda in recent years, and will push hard to allow more extractivist industries in indigenous lands, expand road-building, privatise rivers, weaken environmental protections and possibly attempt to impeach the president.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026.desc: Aston Villa chairman accuses ex-Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher of insulting the club, with legal action threatened.
paras: Aston Villa will pursue legal action ⁠against pundit Jamie ⁠Carragher, the Premier League club has said, accusing the former Liverpool defender of making “unacceptable insults” about the ⁠club and their supporters.

Villa’s response followed comments by Carragher on the Stick to Football podcast, where he told Villa ⁠supporters to “shut the [expletive] up” and said, “Aston Villa will never be Manchester United”, suggesting there is a hierarchy in football.

With Michael Carrick’s role at United in danger after the team’s dismal start to the season, Carragher also discussed speculation linking Villa manager Unai Emery with a move to Old Trafford should the opportunity arise.

pg:https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/foot.desc: Michael Carrick is bidding to save his job in crunch Stamford Bridge clash
paras: The latest Premier League weekend kicks off with a blockbuster showdown as Chelsea host Manchester United at Stamford Bridge. Michael Carrick will be desperate for a positive result to ease the enormous pressure on his job, having surprisingly been offered a stay of execution despite heavy defeats by Como and Bournemouth over the past 10 days that continued a wretched start to the season and appeared to leave his position untenable.

Carrick will be given the chance to rescue the situation, but needs results fast and will have the added stress of co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe being in attendance today. The scrutiny on Chelsea counterpart Xabi Alonso is nowhere near as severe, though he too will be eager to bounce back quickly after the Blues’ winning momentum was halted by a rare home defeat by rivals Tottenham and Carabao Cup penalty heartbreak at Liverpool.

Bruno Fernandes makes a swift return to the Man Utd starting lineup this afternoon and will retain the captaincy after clear-the-air talks with Carrick, while the hosts are boosted by Cole Palmer’s comeback and hand a rare start to Estevao. Follow Chelsea vs Manchester United live below!

pg:https://www.npr.org/2026/10/31/g-s1-1.desc: Ahead of Election Day, listeners send in questions about whether debates are dead, if polls are reliable for election coverage and how Trump might work with Democrats if they win control of Congress.
paras: Voters fill out their ballots at an early voting polling place at Bethel Lutheran Church on October 28, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minn. Stephen Maturen/Getty Images hide caption

Ahead of Election Day, there are a lot of questions about what might happen, what the implications of different outcomes might be and even what it's like to cover elections. In collaboration with the NPR Politics Podcast, listeners sent in their questions about the election and politics for our political correspondents to answer.

This is a common question every election cycle, but it's a little like saying, "I don't like the media because the media is biased." There are good polls and bad polls just like there are good reporters and bad reporters.

paras: Polls are again under scrutiny, with some rushing in to proclaim their demise. But it isn’t that polls have gotten worse. Rather, a mix of factors is creating unprecedented challenges for polling and for the public trying to understand it.

Why? First, there are the perennial challenges that are consistently misunderstood. Surveys are well suited to measure beliefs and attitudes about issues, and they can capture respondents’ candidate preferences pretty accurately. But predicting who will actually turn out to vote will always be an imperfect effort, largely because people are bad at predicting their own behavior and tend to report aspirations rather than realities.

This challenge is magnified in midterms and primaries, contests that often have lower turnout, localized dynamics and low information. And yet, many consumers expect a level of precision that polls can’t deliver. And the cycle of disappointment repeats.
